name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Engineering for Environmental Sustainability and International Cooperation (EESIC)
provider: Erasmus Mundus consortium (University of Trento, IST Lisboa, UPV Valencia)

deadline_notes: The admission page still carried no closing date when rechecked on 7 October 2026. Its exact wording is that the call for applications for the 2027-2029 cohort "will be published on this section in October 2026" - the current month - so a date is expected imminently but had not appeared. The previous 2026-2028 call is published in the site FAQ as a reference, and the site states explicitly that it is only a reference and that all admission information will come from the new call.

benefits: EUR 1,400 monthly allowance
Tuition and mandatory participation costs waived
Mobility across three European universities
Fourth-semester project work with an associated partner
description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in engineering for environmental sustainability and international cooperation, awarding degrees in environmental engineering. Students spend one semester each in Lisbon, Valencia and Trento, then a fourth semester of project work and thesis with an associated partner. The call for the 2027-2029 cohort opens in October 2026.

Travel costs
Installation costs
Living allowance
Tuition fees waived for scholarship holders

name: DAAD Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)

DAAD publishes a course list carrying the 2027/2028 application deadlines. Applicants may apply to a maximum of three courses and must rank them in order of priority.

nationality: Graduates from developing and newly industrialised countries on the DAAD DAC list, which covers Sub-Saharan Africa, South and Central Asia, East Asia, South America, the Near and Middle East and parts of Europe

Academic degrees should normally be no more than six years old. Applicants who have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline cannot be considered. Applications must be sent directly to the chosen course; documents sent to DAAD are not forwarded.

benefits: EUR 992 monthly stipend for master's candidates
Health, accident and personal liability insurance
Travel allowance
Possible monthly rent subsidy
Possible allowance for accompanying family members
Six-month preparatory German course for German-taught courses

amount: The University Composition Fee at the appropriate rate, a maintenance allowance of GBP 23,152 for 12 months at the 2026-27 rate (pro rata for shorter courses, and up to four years for PhD scholars), one economy single airfare at the beginning and end of the course, and inbound visa costs including the Immigration Health Surcharge. Discretionary additions include academic development funding of GBP 750 to GBP 4,000 and a Dependent Children Allowance
deadline_notes: Gates Cambridge publishes no single date: applications are made through the University of Cambridge graduate application, so the deadline is the course-specific Cambridge funding deadline. There are two rounds, a US round and an International round, with roughly a third of the awards in the US round.
duration: One-year postgraduate courses, or PhD study funded for up to four years

nationality: Citizens of any country outside the United Kingdom
eligibility.other: Open to applicants for a full-time or part-time PhD, an MLitt, or a one-year full-time postgraduate course, in any subject available at Cambridge. Undergraduate degrees, MASt courses, part-time degrees other than the PhD, and professional or non-standard degrees such as the MBA, EMBA, MFin and PGCE are not considered. Selection weighs outstanding intellectual ability, reasons for the choice of course, a commitment to improving the lives of others and leadership potential. Around 70 full-cost scholarships are offered each year, about two-thirds of them to PhD students. Applicants already part-way through a course cannot apply to fund the remainder of it.

benefits: Full University Composition Fee
Maintenance allowance of GBP 23,152 for 12 months at the 2026-27 rate
Economy airfare at the start and end of the course
Inbound visa costs and Immigration Health Surcharge
Discretionary academic development funding of GBP 750 to GBP 4,000
Discretionary Dependent Children Allowance
description: Full-cost scholarship at the University of Cambridge for postgraduate students from outside the United Kingdom, in any subject the university offers. Around 70 are awarded each year, roughly two-thirds of them to PhD students. Applications are made through the Cambridge graduate application, so the deadline is the course-specific funding deadline.

name: Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarship
funding_type: Full first-year tuition plus a living-expenses contribution, extended to the second year subject to study progress
amount: Full tuition fees for the first year of a TU Delft MSc programme at the statutory or institutional rate according to the registered nationality, plus a contribution towards living expenses. Second-year allowances require at least 48 of 60 ECTS to have been completed
deadline_notes: The deadline is 1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET for the 2027-2029 intake, and a complete MSc application must already have been submitted by then. Two scholarships are available per faculty, and applicants are informed by the end of March 2027.
duration: Two-year TU Delft MSc programme; the scholarship covers the first year and is extended to the second subject to study progress

nationality: International applicants; tuition is calculated at the statutory or institutional rate according to the applicant's registered nationality

language_requirements.english: An English language certificate must be uploaded with the MSc application before the scholarship deadline

eligibility.other: Applicants must be (conditionally) admitted to one of the two-year regular TU Delft MSc programmes; International Joint Education Programmes are excluded. They must have achieved excellent results in a previous programme relevant to the master's applied for, indicated as being within the top 10% of graduates, although proof of ranking is not required. A complete MSc application, the scholarship application form, one reference letter and the English certificate must all be submitted before the deadline. Scholarship holders may not receive any other partial or full scholarship funding in addition.

benefits: Full first-year tuition at the statutory or institutional rate
Contribution towards living expenses
Second-year allowance subject to completing at least 48 of 60 ECTS
description: Scholarship for excellent international applicants admitted to a two-year regular TU Delft MSc programme, covering first-year tuition and contributing to living expenses. Two are available per faculty, and International Joint Education Programmes are excluded. The deadline for the 2027-2029 intake is 1 December 2026.

name: KTH Scholarship
amount: Covers the full KTH tuition fee for the first and second year, provided first-year study results are satisfactory. Living costs are not included
deadline_notes: Applications open on 1 December 2026 and close on 15 January 2027, with results announced on 1 April 2027. Supporting documents for the underlying master's application must be submitted by 2 February.
duration: One or two-year master's programme; the waiver covers both years subject to satisfactory first-year results

nationality: Open to fee-paying international students; the scholarship covers the tuition fee charged to fee-paying students
eligibility.other: Applicants must be fee-paying students who have applied to a KTH master's programme as their first priority and paid the application fee; programmes listed as second, third or fourth priority cannot be funded. Available for all master's programmes with two years spent at KTH, the joint master's programmes in Molecular Techniques in Life Science and in Biostatistics and Data Science, and the one-year master's in Architectural Lighting Design. Joint Erasmus+ and EIT programmes are not eligible, nor is Computer Simulations for Science and Engineering; applicants to those may instead apply for the KTH Joint Programme Scholarship. Selection weighs grades, the ranking of the degree-awarding university, research experience or publications, relevant work experience, and a stated contribution to sustainable development. In 2026, 65 of 718 admitted applicants (9%) were nominated.

benefits: Full tuition fee for the first year
Full tuition fee for the second year, subject to satisfactory results
No additional documents required beyond the master's application
description: Merit-based tuition fee waiver at KTH Royal Institute of Technology covering the full fee for a one or two-year master's programme. Applicants must apply to a KTH master's as their first priority and be fee-paying students. The 2027 application window runs from 1 December 2026 to 15 January 2027.

name: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships
provider: Swiss Confederation, Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS/ESKAS)
university: Any Swiss cantonal university, university of applied sciences, ETH Zurich or EPFL, or an institute of the ETH Domain (PSI, WSL, Empa, Eawag)
amount: CHF 2,450 per month, for a research stay of 12 months or a PhD of 36 months. Maximum age 35 at the time of application
deadline_notes: Applications opened on 20 August 2026 for the 2027-2028 academic year. Deadlines are set by country of origin and published by the Swiss diplomatic representation handling the application, so there is no single date. Decisions are announced by the end of May.
duration: 12 months for a research stay, or 36 months for a PhD

nationality: Open to applicants from 183 countries; applications are submitted to the Swiss diplomatic representation in the applicant's country
eligibility.other: Intended for early career researchers who have already completed a master's degree. The application must be supported by an academic supervisor in Switzerland willing to direct the proposed research. Selection is assessed on the candidate profile, the quality of the research project, and the potential for future research cooperation. Applying is free of charge; the issuing body warns against phishing offers that use the programme's name to request payment.

benefits: CHF 2,450 monthly allowance
Research stay or PhD funding
Placement at a Swiss university, ETH Zurich, EPFL or an ETH Domain institute
description: Swiss Confederation scholarships for early career researchers from 183 countries who already hold a master's degree, funding a 12-month research stay or a 36-month PhD at a Swiss university, ETH Zurich, EPFL or an ETH Domain institute. The application must be backed by a supervisor in Switzerland, and deadlines are set by country of origin.

name: Université Paris-Saclay International Master's Scholarship
university: Université Paris-Saclay and its constituent institutions (AgroParisTech, CentraleSupélec, ENS Paris-Saclay, INSTN-CEA, IOGS, Université Évry Paris-Saclay, UVSQ)
funding_type: Merit-based scholarship for a master's programme
amount: EUR 10,000 per year, paid monthly from September to June, plus a yearly flat fee of up to EUR 900 towards travel and visa costs depending on the country of origin. The amount is reduced during months spent abroad or on internships outside Paris-Saclay laboratories
deadline_notes: The published dates are for the 2026 cycle: master's programme coordinators selected candidates by 25 March 2026 and the scholarship application, with recommendations, closed on 31 March 2026, with results in mid-May. Equivalent dates for the following cycle were not published when this record was checked.
duration: One academic year, automatically renewed for a second year for M1 laureates admitted to an M2 programme

nationality: Open to students of foreign nationality; applicants must be enrolling in a French higher education institution for the first time, excluding exchange programmes and Erasmus Mundus joint masters without a French degree
eligibility.other: Applicants must be under 30 years of age during the year of application and admitted to an eligible master's programme at Université Paris-Saclay before the programme coordinator's deadline; late applications are not accepted. All academic fields are eligible, and all master's programmes except vocational apprenticeships. The scholarship cannot be combined with the France Excellence Eiffel or France Excellence Europa scholarships, nor with an Erasmus Mundus scholarship, and applicants receiving other funding above EUR 600 per month are ineligible. Payment is made only on arrival and after registration; no advance payment is possible.

benefits: EUR 10,000 per year paid monthly
Travel and visa flat fee of up to EUR 900
Automatic renewal for a second year for M1 laureates
Support with administrative procedures and the accommodation search
description: Scholarship of EUR 10,000 per year for international students admitted to a master's programme at Université Paris-Saclay, in any academic field. Applicants must be under 30 and enrolling in France for the first time, and cannot hold an Eiffel, France Excellence Europa or Erasmus Mundus scholarship at the same time.

name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Mechanics of Sustainable Materials and Structures (MS²)
university: TU Dortmund University (Germany), University of Trento (Italy) and École Centrale de Nantes (France)
amount: About EUR 1,400 per month for two years, with full tuition fees covered
deadline_notes: The funding page states the application period runs from 1 January to 15 March, but writes the year as a placeholder ('20XY'), so no specific year is published. Admission and the scholarship are separate procedures: applicants must also apply to TU Dortmund's master's admissions in parallel.
duration: Two years (120 ECTS) across three countries, awarded as a multiple degree by the participating institutions

nationality: Open to applicants of any nationality; scholarships are awarded on a competitive basis
eligibility.other: Selection is scored on two reference letters (15 points) and a motivation letter of up to two pages (10 points), among other criteria. The programme is run by the architecture and civil engineering faculties of the three universities, and covers advanced mechanics for innovative materials and structures, materials and structures under extreme conditions, and related areas. Exact bachelor's subject requirements were not stated on the pages checked.

benefits: About EUR 1,400 per month for two years
Full tuition fees covered
Study across Germany, Italy and France
Multiple degree from three universities
description: Erasmus Mundus joint master's in the mechanics of sustainable materials and structures, taught by TU Dortmund, the University of Trento and École Centrale de Nantes. Funding is about EUR 1,400 per month for two years with tuition covered. The published application window is 1 January to 15 March, but the site does not state the year.

name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Risk Assessment and Management of Civil Infrastructures (NORISK)
city: Guimarães, Barcelona, Padova and La Rochelle
university: University of Minho (Portugal, coordinator), Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (Spain), University of Padova (Italy) and La Rochelle Université (France)
amount: EUR 1,400 per month for the duration of the programme, plus the full EUR 9,000 participation cost. Up to seven scholarships a year are reserved for Partner Country students, three for Programme Country students, three financed by NDICI and one by IPA
deadline_notes: The 2026/2027 intake ran three calls, closing on 30 January, 15 April and 15 May 2026, all now passed. Erasmus Mundus scholarships are available only in the first call. Dates for the next intake were not published when this record was checked.
duration: Two years starting 1 October, with three compulsory mobility periods and one optional workshop across Portugal, Spain, Italy and France

nationality: Open to applicants of any nationality; separate scholarship quotas apply to Programme Country and Partner Country applicants, and Nepal falls in the Partner Country group
eligibility.other: Requires at least 240 ECTS of prior study in civil engineering, industrial or systems engineering, materials engineering, environmental engineering or a related field. A mobility track including Padova requires 300 ECTS with specified subject credits, including 6 ECTS each in hydraulics, hydraulic and marine constructions, structural mechanics and structural engineering, 4 ECTS in geotechnics, and further credits in civil engineering, mathematics, physics or chemistry. English: TOEFL 525 paper-based or 72 internet-based, or IELTS 6.5. A EUR 250 deposit confirms acceptance and is refunded on enrolment. Five per cent of grants are reserved for women and five per cent for students with special educational needs. Between five and seven applicants from any one country are called to interview.

benefits: EUR 1,400 per month for the whole programme
Full EUR 9,000 participation cost covered, so no tuition is charged
Up to seven scholarships a year reserved for Partner Country students
Consortium scholarships of EUR 9,000 covering tuition
Health insurance included in the participation cost
description: Erasmus Mundus joint master's in the risk assessment and management of civil infrastructures, taught across Portugal, Spain, Italy and France. Scholarships are EUR 1,400 per month with the EUR 9,000 participation cost fully covered, and up to seven a year are reserved for Partner Country students. Applicants need at least 240 ECTS in civil, materials, environmental or industrial engineering.

name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Advanced Structural Analysis and Design using Composite Materials (FRP++)
university: University of Minho (Portugal), University of Girona (Spain), University of Naples Federico II (Italy) and INSA Toulouse (France)
amount: EUR 1,400 per month for the duration of the programme, plus the full EUR 9,000 participation cost. Consortium scholarships of EUR 9,000, EUR 6,500 and EUR 4,500 are also offered
deadline_notes: The fifth edition runs in 2026/2027 with three calls that closed on 31 January, 14 June and 15 July 2026. EU scholarships are available only in the first call. The scholarships page still describes a 'third edition in 2024/2025' while the applications page says fifth edition 2026/2027; the applications page is the more current of the two. Dates for the next intake were not published when this record was checked.
duration: Two years starting 1 October, with three compulsory mobility periods and one optional workshop across Portugal, Spain, Italy and France

nationality: Open to applicants of any nationality, with separate scholarship quotas for Programme Country and Partner Country applicants. Nepal is listed explicitly among both the Partner Countries and the NDICI partner countries.
eligibility.other: Requires a degree in civil engineering, mechanical or industrial engineering, materials engineering, aeronautical engineering, polymers engineering or a related field. A bachelor's with 240 ECTS is accepted, or 300 ECTS for mobility tracks including Naples. English: TOEFL 525 paper-based or 72 internet-based, or IELTS 6.5, with the certificate less than three years old; applicants without a certificate may still apply but score lower and will be interviewed to verify their English. Five per cent of grants are reserved for women and five per cent for students with special educational needs. A deposit confirms acceptance, with a minimum charge of EUR 250.

benefits: EUR 1,400 per month for the whole programme
Full EUR 9,000 participation cost covered, so no tuition is charged
Up to seven scholarships a year for Partner Country applicants, with Nepal explicitly eligible
Consortium scholarships of EUR 9,000, EUR 6,500 and EUR 4,500
Health insurance included in the participation cost
description: Erasmus Mundus joint master's in advanced structural analysis and design using composite materials, taught across Portugal, Spain, Italy and France. Scholarships are EUR 1,400 per month with the EUR 9,000 participation cost covered. Nepal appears explicitly on the programme's Partner Country and NDICI lists, so applicants qualify for the Partner Country quota.

name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Flood Risk Management (FRM)
university: IHE Delft Institute for Water Education (Netherlands, coordinator), TU Dresden (Germany), Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (Spain) and University of Ljubljana (Slovenia)
amount: EUR 1,400 per month for up to 24 months, covering subsistence, accommodation, travel and installation, plus the participation costs including tuition and full insurance. Standard tuition is EUR 18,000
deadline_notes: The Erasmus Mundus scholarship deadline is 3 January 2027 at 23:59 Dutch time for applicants from Partner Countries, which includes Nepal; applicants from Programme and IPA countries have until 7 February 2027. English test results may be uploaded as late as 1 February 2027 provided the application itself is submitted by 3 January 2027. Scholarship outcomes are announced in early April 2027. A separate reduced-fee scholarship, EUR 3,000 instead of EUR 18,000, closes on 15 April 2027.
duration: Two years (24 months), four semesters across Germany, the Netherlands, Spain and Slovenia, ending in a research thesis

nationality: Open to applicants of any nationality, with separate scholarship quotas for Programme Country and Partner Country applicants; Nepal is in the Partner Country group
eligibility.other: Requires a first degree equivalent to at least 180 ECTS in civil or environmental engineering, geosciences, environmental sciences, limnology, oceanography, geography, geology or natural resources, with academic knowledge of mathematics and water-related subjects. Minimum GPA of B or B+ on the US system, or a 2nd upper classification on the UK system. An internationally recognised English language test is required. Applications may be submitted before the degree is completed if at least 120 ECTS have been passed, provided the degree is finished by 15 August. Eight further scholarships are reserved for NDICI countries and four for IPA countries, the latter with a deadline of 7 March 2027.

benefits: EUR 1,400 per month for up to 24 months
Participation costs covered, including tuition, library, laboratory and full insurance
No separate scholarship application — it is part of the admission form
Additional places reserved for NDICI and IPA country applicants
A reduced-fee route (EUR 3,000 instead of EUR 18,000) for applicants who miss the scholarship
description: Erasmus Mundus joint master's in flood risk management, coordinated by IHE Delft with TU Dresden, Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya and the University of Ljubljana. Civil engineering is an accepted first degree. Scholarships pay EUR 1,400 per month for up to 24 months plus all participation costs, and the deadline for applicants from Nepal's category is 3 January 2027.

name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Groundwater and Global Change — Impacts and Adaptation (GroundwatCH)
university: IHE Delft Institute for Water Education (Netherlands, coordinator), TU Dresden (Germany) and Instituto Superior Técnico, Universidade de Lisboa (Portugal)
amount: EUR 1,400 per month for 24 months, covering subsistence, travel and installation, plus the participation costs including tuition, library and laboratory costs and full insurance
deadline_notes: The Erasmus Mundus scholarship deadline is 3 January 2027 at 23:59 Dutch time for applicants from Partner Countries, which includes Nepal; applicants from Programme Countries have until 7 February 2027. Applicants who do not yet hold an English test result may upload it as late as 1 February 2027 and still be considered for a scholarship. Admission and scholarship outcomes are announced in April 2027. Applications arriving after the scholarship deadline are still considered for academic admission but not for the scholarship, and applicants funding their own studies must apply and confirm funding by 15 April 2027. About 15 scholarships a year are awarded across roughly four intakes, around 60 in total for intakes starting between 2024 and 2027.
duration: Two years (120 ECTS), taught in English across the Netherlands, Germany and Portugal

nationality: Open to applicants of any nationality, with separate scholarship lists for Programme Country and Partner Country applicants; Nepal is in the Partner Country group
eligibility.gpa_minimum: CGPA of at least B/B+ on the US system, or a 2nd upper classification on the UK system
eligibility.other: Requires a first degree equivalent to at least 180 ECTS. A bachelor degree in geologic, hydraulic, civil, environmental or agricultural engineering, geosciences, environmental sciences, climate sciences, geography, geology or a similar subject is accepted — civil engineering is named explicitly. Sufficient academic knowledge of mathematics is required. Applications may be submitted before the degree is finished if at least 120 ECTS are complete, provided the degree is awarded by 15 August of the year the programme starts. Students who have previously held an EMJM scholarship are not eligible.

benefits: EUR 1,400 per month for the full two years
Participation costs covered, including tuition, library and laboratory costs and full insurance
No separate scholarship application — the scholarship is requested inside the admission form
Around 15 scholarships a year, open to Partner and Programme Country applicants alike
Joint degree accredited in each consortium country
description: Erasmus Mundus joint master's in groundwater and global change, coordinated by IHE Delft with TU Dresden and IST Lisbon. Civil engineering is named explicitly among the accepted first degrees. Scholarships pay EUR 1,400 per month for two years plus all participation costs, and the deadline for applicants from Nepal's category is 3 January 2027.

name: EMerald Master in Georesources Engineering
university: Université de Liège (Belgium, coordinator), Université de Lorraine (France), Luleå University of Technology (Sweden) and TU Bergakademie Freiberg (Germany)
amount: EUR 33,600 in total, paid as 24 monthly allowances of EUR 1,400, plus the participation costs paid directly to the coordinating university
deadline_notes: The Erasmus Mundus scholarship round for the 2027 intake opened on 3 November 2026 and closes on 28 February 2027; the 40 highest-rated applicants are invited to interview and every candidate is told the outcome on 16 April 2027. Self-funded applicants apply in a second round with no published closing date, non-EU candidates interviewed in May and EU candidates in July. Only the Erasmus Mundus scholarship is available for this call — the EUR 15,000 EIT RawMaterials grant is marked not available for 2027. Incomplete application forms are not considered.
duration: Two years (120 ECTS), fully taught in English, with each student hosted by at least two of the four partner universities

nationality: Open to applicants worldwide; the Erasmus Mundus scholarship is awarded without a nationality quota
eligibility.other: At least 22.5 ECTS of university-level mathematics is required, because the programme awards an engineering diploma. Two routes qualify: a bachelor degree in engineering with basic knowledge of geology, or one of a listed set of degrees — minerals, mining, chemical, geological or metallurgical engineering, materials engineering oriented towards metals extraction and processing, or a master degree in geology. Civil engineering is not named explicitly and would qualify only through the general engineering route, so applicants from a civil background should expect to evidence geology coursework. A one-page CV and a motivation video are required, and the motivation letter must not be written with AI tools. Students who have previously held an EMJM scholarship are not eligible.

benefits: EUR 1,400 per month for 24 months, EUR 33,600 in total
Travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs covered
Participation costs paid directly to the coordinating university
Awarded only in full, to full-time students
Non-European self-funded students pay EUR 8,000 a year and may request a fee waiver
description: Erasmus Mundus and EIT-labelled joint master's in georesources engineering, coordinated by the Université de Liège with partners in France, Sweden and Germany. It balances geology and mineral-resource knowledge with process engineering, and the Erasmus Mundus scholarship is worth EUR 33,600 over two years. The 2027 scholarship round runs from 3 November 2026 to 28 February 2027.

name: Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks (MSCA-DN)
region: European Union member states and Horizon Europe associated countries
city: Varies by project — each funded network recruits at its own partner institutions
university: International consortia of at least three independent organisations from different EU member states or Horizon Europe associated countries, combining universities, research institutions and companies; further partners may join from any country in the world
funding_type: Salaried doctoral position funded by the European Union
amount: A living allowance plus a mobility allowance, and where applicable family, long-term leave and special-needs allowances; the exact salary is set by the recruiting institution and its country
deadline_notes: There is no single application deadline, and that is the important point: Doctoral Networks recruit continuously. Each funded project advertises its own PhD vacancies and candidates apply to those vacancies directly, most of them listed on the EURAXESS portal, which is updated daily. What runs to a calendar is the call for the consortia themselves — the 2026 Doctoral Networks call is open with a proposal deadline of 24 November 2026 at 17:00 CET — because new vacancies appear as each call's projects begin recruiting. A candidate should therefore monitor EURAXESS rather than wait for a date.
duration: Each fellowship runs between 3 and 36 months, or between 3 and 48 months for a Joint Doctorate; the networks themselves last up to four years, or five for Joint Doctorates

nationality: Candidates may be of any nationality, including Nepali
eligibility.other: Candidates must not already hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment, and must be enrolled in a doctoral programme during the project. A mobility rule applies: in general the candidate must not have lived or worked in the country of the recruiting organisation for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before recruitment. Industrial Doctorates additionally require at least 50% of the researcher's time to be spent outside academia. Requirements specific to each post — degree subject, grades, language — are set by the recruiting project, not centrally.

benefits: A living allowance and a separate mobility allowance, paid as an employment contract
Family, long-term leave and special-needs allowances where applicable
Fully funded research, training and networking budget
Secondments with other partners in the network, including industry
Open to any nationality, with no quota by country
description: The European Union scheme that funds salaried PhD positions across international research consortia. Unlike a scholarship it has no single deadline — projects advertise vacancies continuously on the EURAXESS portal and candidates apply to individual posts. Open to any nationality, with a mobility rule that the candidate must not have spent more than 12 months of the previous 36 in the recruiting country.

name: Knight-Hennessy Scholars (Stanford University)
funding_type: Full graduate fellowship, held alongside a Stanford degree programme
amount: Funding for up to three years: a fellowship applied to tuition and associated fees, a stipend for living and academic expenses such as room and board, books, supplies and local transport, a travel stipend covering one annual economy-class round trip to Stanford, and a one-time relocation stipend for newly enrolling scholars. Scholars in their second and third years may apply for supplemental academic-enrichment funds. Where a degree runs longer than three years — as a PhD usually does — the department funds the remaining years, so the fellowship itself does not cover a full doctorate.
deadline_notes: The application to join the 2027 cohort closed on 6 October 2026 at 13:00 Pacific Time, and the 2028 cohort application opens in summer 2027. The Knight-Hennessy application is separate from, and runs concurrently with, the Stanford degree-programme application, which carries its own departmental deadline — a candidate must be accepted by and enrol in a full-time Stanford graduate programme to take up the fellowship.
duration: The fellowship funds up to three years of graduate study; a PhD is normally funded by the department for the years beyond that

nationality: No restriction by nationality. The programme states that it encourages citizens and residents of all countries to apply and sets no quotas by discipline, programme or world region, and it does not require an institutional endorsement.
eligibility.other: Two baseline requirements. First, the applicant must apply to, be accepted by and enrol in a full-time Stanford graduate degree programme starting the same year as the fellowship, which means a second, separate application. Second, the first bachelor's degree must have been earned in January 2020 or later for the 2027 cohort, a window extended by two years for applicants who served in the military; applicants completing a first degree by September 2027 are also eligible. Stanford programmes excluded from the fellowship are the Honors Cooperative Program, the Master of Liberal Arts, the JSD and MLS law degrees, coterminal degrees, and a current PhD student adding an MA or MS in the same discipline.

benefits: Tuition and associated fees covered for up to three years
A stipend for living and academic expenses
One annual economy-class round trip to Stanford
A one-time relocation stipend on enrolment
No nationality quota and no institutional endorsement required
A multidisciplinary community of scholars across every Stanford graduate programme
description: Stanford's flagship graduate fellowship, open to citizens and residents of every country with no quotas by discipline or region, funding up to three years of any full-time Stanford graduate degree including a master's or PhD in civil and environmental engineering. It requires a separate, concurrent application to the Stanford degree programme and a first bachelor's degree earned in January 2020 or later. The 2027 cohort application closed on 6 October 2026; the 2028 cycle opens in summer 2027.

name: Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program
provider: Fulbright / U.S. Department of State, administered in Nepal by the Commission for Educational Exchange between the United States and Nepal
university: Selected U.S. host universities, assigned by the programme rather than chosen by the applicant
amount: Covers a ten- to twelve-month programme of academic study at a U.S. host university plus a professional affiliation placement. The official programme pages and the Nepal country page consulted describe the structure of the award but do not publish a stipend figure, so no amount is recorded here.
deadline_notes: Deadlines are set per country and are not published centrally — the programme states only that applicants must apply through their Binational Fulbright Commission or the Public Affairs Section of the U.S. Embassy, and that deadlines vary by country. In Nepal the programme is administered by the Commission for Educational Exchange between the United States and Nepal, whose Humphrey page states that applications for the 2026-27 cohort are closed and that a new announcement is pending, so no date is recorded.
duration: Ten to twelve months of academic study and professional affiliation in the United States

nationality: Nepal appears on the programme eligibility list under the South and Central Asia region, which spans 148 countries and regions; in Nepal the programme is administered by the Binational Fulbright Commission
eligibility.other: Requires a bachelor's degree or equivalent, a minimum of five years of full-time professional experience, demonstrated leadership and a record of public service, demonstrated English ability, and limited prior experience in the United States. It awards no degree: fellows design an individual programme of academic study and professional affiliation instead of enrolling in one. Fields are grouped into four impact areas, of which Sustainable Lands covers Agricultural and Rural Development, Natural Resources, Sustainability and Environmental Policy, and Urban and Regional Planning — policy and planning subjects adjacent to civil and environmental engineering rather than engineering degrees themselves.

benefits: Ten to twelve months in the United States at a designated host university
A professional affiliation placement with a U.S. organisation in the fellow’s field
Academic study designed around the fellow’s own objectives rather than a fixed curriculum
Leadership training and access to a network of more than 6,600 fellows from 163 countries
Administered in Nepal by the Binational Fulbright Commission, which sets the national deadline
description: A non-degree Fulbright fellowship for mid-career professionals, running ten to twelve months at a U.S. host university with a professional affiliation placement. Nepal is on the eligible-country list and the programme is administered there by the Binational Fulbright Commission. The fields most relevant to a civil engineer are under the Sustainable Lands impact area — natural resources and environmental policy, and urban and regional planning. It requires five years of full-time professional experience, and the 2026-27 cohort is closed with the next announcement pending.
